page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; running head at top centre; page number at top left; no margin notes; one short catchword-free foot line at the bottom right, which is a catchword "strant" printed as "strant" at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: Melchior Inchoferus, omniáque regna Occiden-talia clarè demonstrant. Quantum Hetrusca & Latina hodierna ab antiqua recesserint, ex inscri-ptionibus & Tabulis Eugubinis Hetruscis literis antiquis exaratis, & ex columnis rostratis, quas nemo adhuc explicavit, cuivis constat; quantaque ex variarum gentium sinitimarum confluxu oriantur corruptelæ, in omnibus Europæ linguis quotidiè conspicimus, ut bene observat doctiss. Kircherus. Idcirco linguæ omnes, quas libri scripti à communi clade non servant, vicissitudini, ut omnia humana, semper obnoxiæ sunt, & singulis seculis insignem mutationem subeunt.

12. De Hebraica tamen, ut observant quidam, hoc maximè notandum, eam esse omnium purlis-simam sine ulla vocum peregrinarum mixtura, quæ in Chaldæa & Syra frequentissima; esse quoque Chaldaicâ multò simpliciorem, ideóque antiquiorem, cùm Chaldaica multa vocabula inter se diversissima ad unicam radicem Hebraicam reducantur.

13. Antiqua autem hujus-linguæ elegantiam & utilitatem prædicare idem ferè esset ac Soli facem accendere. Elegantiam ejus suprà Græcam & Latinam fusè ostendit Erpenius eleganti de hac lingua oratione, orat. scil. 3. p. 106, 107, &c. Juásq; veneres habere, maximè dum de sacris agitur, quas cætera linguæ exprimere non valent, nõrunt omnes: vix ulla est lingua ex hac non prognata, ut in reliquis linguis Orientalibus clarum; imò pleráq; Græca Themata originis esse Hebraicæ ostendit idem Erpenius dictâ oratione: literárum-que tum nomina tum ordinem in Alphabeto, in omnibus ferè linguis, ab Hebraâ fluxisse, demon-strant

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "purlis-simam" in the line "omnium purlis-" should read "purifsi-" (the scan shows purifsi-mam); "simpliciorem" and "seculis" in the sixth line of the first paragraph are read as printed, with "singulis seculis" possibly "singulis seculis" (the scan shows "singulis seculis"). The "strant" catchword is a repetition of the line-end word "demon-strant". Long s is rendered as s throughout; hyphenated line-end words kept with printed hyphen. The "/" mark after "reducantur." and the "s" mark in the margin are not text. Reference "orat. scil. 3. p. 106, 107, &c." is in the text as printed, with "scil." possibly "fcil." on the scan; left as printed. Italic words in the scan are marked only where clearly italic. Greek is absent from this page.
